newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Aquino says ready to march against charter change.
newsitem.headline: Aquino says ready to march against charter change.

text.p: Former Philippine President Corazon Aquino, who helped lead the revolt that ousted the late Ferdinand Marcos, said on Monday she was prepared to lead a protest march to oppose moves to change the constitution.

A top aide to President Fidel Ramos said at the weekend that many members of Ramos's People Power (Lakas) favoured amending the constitution to allow Ramos to remain in office for "at least" one more term.
"I have stated categorically so many times before that I am against any amendments at this time because it will be so divisive," Aquino told Reuters by phone.
"If it is necessary, then I will lead a march against amending the constitution," she added.
Aquino electrified the world in 1986 when she helped lead a popular revolt that ended Marcos' 20 years in office and catapulted her to power.
Since stepping down in 1992 she has remained in the political background, but many Filipinos continue to regard her as a moral force in one of Asia's rowdiest democracies.

Ramos has repeatedly said he would not seek a second term. But his executive secretary, Ruben Torres, sparked an uproar in political circles when he told reporters on Saturday that Lakas party members would try to convince Ramos to change his mind.
"If the demand is overwhelming, maybe he will bow to it," Torres said.
Ramos, whose six-year term ends in June 1998, said on Sunday that Torres was merely talking out loud.
"Secretary Torres is really just stating his personal opinion because we have not taken any official stand in Lakas," he told reporters in northern Baguio city. "Let's just wait."

Vice-President Joseph Estrada, seen by many politicians as the strongest opposition bet in elections next year to choose Ramos's successor, said on Sunday he would lead a nationwide campaign to oppose charter amendments.
The constitutional convention that framed the 1987 charter fixed a one-term limit for the president as a safeguard against the rise of authoritarian rule similar to that of Marcos.
